evals.name: review-sync-transaction-trace
evals.prompt: I built `review-sync`: it posts an AI review's findings to the GitHub PR as inline comments and keeps track of what was posted, plus a resync that detects comments deleted on GitHub. It's a bigger change — code is in {FIXTURE}/server/src (modules/review-sync/**, db/schema/review-sync.ts, db/tx.ts, platform/transaction.ts). Please do a thorough architecture review before I open the PR: what's in the wrong place, what breaks our backend rules, and what exactly should change?
evals.expected_output: Finds both transaction-boundary violations hidden behind helper calls (new rule 9), two older layering violations, does not flag the correct resync() flow, and shows the call chain.

assertions.text: Flags that ReviewSyncService.sync() makes GitHub network calls inside the open transaction (tx.run callback → postPlanned → CommentPublisher.publishAll → createReviewComment) and says to post the comments outside the transaction (before it, or after commit / via an outbox job)

Flags that sync() calls jobs.enqueue inside the transaction (via scheduleRecheck) and says to enqueue after commit (JobRunner writes with its own connection / the job may run before commit or survive a rollback)

Flags that mappers.ts imports drizzle-orm (and/eq/SQL) and db/schema to build where-clauses (runScope, commentsOfPr); says mappers may import row types only and these query helpers belong in repository.ts

Flags that domain/dedupe.ts imports FindingRow from db/rows (domain ring depends on infrastructure row types); says to type it with a plain/contract type such as SyncFinding or a local { file, startLine, title }

Does NOT report resync() as a transaction violation — it fetches from GitHub before tx.run and enqueues after the transaction, which is the correct pattern (passes if resync is not flagged or is explicitly called correct)
For the GitHub-in-transaction problem, names at least one intermediate hop of the call chain (postPlanned and/or CommentPublisher.publishAll), not just 'sync uses the network'
